chunks: Remember, when Abraham said: "O Lord, show me how you raise the dead," He said: "What! Do you not believe?" "I do," answered Abraham. "I only ask for my heart's assurance." (The Lord) said: "Trap four birds and tame them, then put each of them on a (separate) hill, and call them, and they will come flying to you. Know that God is all-powerful and all-wise."

key_terms.لِيَطْمَئِنَ قَلْبِي: for my heart to be at ease

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Abraham witness the resurrection of the dead?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the distinction between Abraham’s initial doubt (or seeking confirmation) and his ultimate certainty, illustrating that even prophets require spiritual reassurance. The command to scatter bird parts on hills symbolizes the ease of resurrection for God, while the birds’ eager return signifies the soul's readiness to obey the Creator's call. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for bodily resurrection in Islamic theology, emphasizing that faith is not merely intellectual but requires heart-felt tranquility.
